title.en: Endocrine glands: pituitary, thyroid and parathyroid

text.en: The body has a second control system besides the nerves. Ductless glands pour hormones into the blood and each hormone acts on specific target organs.

Hormones are chemical messengers made in minute amounts by ductless endocrine glands and carried by the blood to target organs; exocrine glands such as salivary and sweat glands have ducts.
Thomas Addison is the Father of Endocrinology; Bayliss and Starling introduced the term hormone in 1909 after discovering secretin.
The pituitary lies at the base of the midbrain attached to the hypothalamus and is the master gland because it controls other glands.
The anterior pituitary secretes growth hormone, TSH, ACTH, gonadotropins FSH and LH, and prolactin.
Too little growth hormone in children causes dwarfism, too much causes gigantism, and too much in adults causes acromegaly.
The posterior pituitary releases ADH (vasopressin), which increases water reabsorption in the kidney, and oxytocin, which contracts the uterus and ejects milk.
Lack of ADH causes diabetes insipidus with a large urine output.
The thyroid has two lobes joined by an isthmus and makes T3 and thyroxine T4 using iodine and tyrosine; they regulate basal metabolic rate and body temperature.
Iodine deficiency causes simple goitre; low thyroid hormone causes cretinism in children and myxoedema in adults; excess causes Grave's disease with protruding eyes.
The four parathyroid glands make parathormone, which regulates calcium and phosphorus; low levels cause tetany.

problem.en: Why do people in iodine-poor hill regions often develop goitre?

text.en: The thyroid needs iodine to make thyroxine.

why.en: Iodine is part of T3 and T4.

text.en: With too little iodine the thyroid cannot make enough hormone.

why.en: The pituitary then stimulates it more.

text.en: The gland enlarges, forming a swelling in the neck called goitre.

prompt.en: Why is the pituitary called the master gland? Give two examples.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking the pituitary is in the thyroid or kidney

points.en: Pituitary = master gland: GH, TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH, PRL, ADH, oxytocin.
Thyroid needs iodine: goitre, cretinism, myxoedema, Grave's.
Parathormone controls calcium: low gives tetany.
